questions.q: TOGAF treats the enterprise as which of the following?
questions.e: TOGAF treats the enterprise as a system. You can develop one EA for a whole corporation or several independent EAs for divisions, depending on goals and resources.

questions.q: Which architecture domain describes the structure of an organization's conceptual, logical, and physical data assets?
questions.e: The Data Architecture describes the structure of the organization's conceptual, logical, and physical data assets and data management resources.

questions.q: According to the TOGAF Standard, how can architecture abstraction be used?
o: To eliminate the need for building blocks
To divide a problem into smaller, easier-to-model areas
questions.e: Abstraction is a technique for dividing a problem into smaller, easier-to-model areas, layered high-to-detailed across all four domains (contextual, conceptual, logical, physical).

questions.q: On the Architecture Continuum, what sits at the generic (left) end?
questions.e: The Architecture Continuum runs from generic (left) foundation and industry-wide architectures to organization-specific (right) architectures adapted for the enterprise.

questions.q: Which part of the Architecture Repository holds guidelines, templates, patterns, reference models, and the viewpoint library?
questions.e: The Reference Library holds guidelines, templates, patterns, reference architectures and models, and the viewpoint library.

questions.q: How is the top-level structure of the TOGAF Content Framework organized?
o: By the levels of the Enterprise Continuum
It mirrors the phases of the ADM
questions.e: The Content Framework's top-level structure mirrors the ADM phases, acting as a companion to the ADM and defining which work products to develop.

questions.q: An Architecture Capability is best described as which of the following?
o: A catalog of reusable building blocks
A business capability for architecture, run with its own management functions
questions.e: An Architecture Capability is a business capability for architecture, comprising organization structures, roles, skills, responsibilities, and processes, run like an operational unit.

questions.q: From which body does TOGAF draw its risk management concepts, with risk driven top-down from business value?
questions.e: TOGAF uses risk concepts from the SABSA Institute, with risk driven top-down from business value.

questions.q: According to the notes, what is the most critical source of gaps identified during gap analysis?
questions.e: Ignored stakeholder concerns are the most critical source of gaps. A gap states what must change between baseline and target.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly names ADM Phases B, C, and D in order?
questions.e: Phase B is Business Architecture, Phase C is Information Systems Architectures (Data and Application), and Phase D is Technology Architecture.

questions.q: What does a 'draft' version numbering status indicate about a deliverable?
o: It has been reviewed and signed off
It is under development with no formal review or approval yet
It has been archived in the repository
questions.e: Draft means the deliverable is under development with no formal review or approval yet. Approved means reviewed and approved, but not necessarily finalized.

questions.q: The 'crop circle' ADM graphic is best understood as which of the following?
o: A mandated activity sequence that must be followed strictly
A stylized representation of essential information flow, not a process model
A project schedule with fixed dates
The organization chart of the EA team
questions.e: The ADM graphic is a stylized path showing essential information flow, not a process model or mandated activity sequence.

questions.q: Which pair are the two objectives of the Preliminary Phase?
o: Determine the capability desired, and establish the capability
Develop the vision, and obtain approval to proceed
Draft the roadmap, and finalize the plan
questions.e: The two Preliminary Phase objectives are to determine the architecture capability desired and to establish the architecture capability.

questions.q: Which document triggers the move from the Preliminary Phase into Phase A?
questions.e: The Request for Architecture Work, an order from the sponsoring organization to the architecture team, triggers the move from Preliminary to Phase A.

questions.q: Which ADM phase develops the baseline and target Business Architecture?
questions.e: Phase B develops the baseline and target Business Architecture, covering business strategy, governance, organization, and key processes.

questions.q: In which ADM phase are Transition Architectures first determined?
questions.e: Phase E, Opportunities and Solutions, performs initial implementation planning and determines the Transition Architectures.

questions.q: Which activity is central to Phase F, Migration Planning?
o: Transitioning governance from developing to realizing the EA and finalizing the plan
questions.e: Phase F finalizes the detailed Implementation and Migration Plan and transitions governance from developing to realizing the EA.

questions.q: In which ADM phase does the TOGAF Standard align with Agile development, setting constraints for product owners and defining the enterprise backlog?
questions.e: TOGAF aligns with Agile in Phase G. EA identifies products and boundaries, sets constraints for product owners, and defines the enterprise backlog.

questions.q: Which input is the most important architectural trigger for Phase H, Architecture Change Management?
questions.e: The Change Request is the most important architectural input to Phase H; it triggers change management and can kick-start a further cycle of architecture work.

questions.q: Which statement about the Requirements Management phase is correct?
o: It connects to every ADM phase including Preliminary
It connects to every phase except Preliminary and runs continuously
It runs only once, between Phases A and B
It replaces the need for governance
questions.e: Requirements Management sits at the centre, connects to every phase except Preliminary, and runs continuously throughout the cycle.

questions.q: How do the ADM Techniques relate to the ADM itself?
o: They provide supporting guidelines and techniques used when applying the ADM
They are only used in the Preliminary Phase
They are mandatory in every phase
questions.e: ADM Techniques provide supporting guidelines and techniques (such as principles, gap analysis, risk management) used when applying the ADM.

questions.q: TOGAF distinguishes two levels of principles. How do architecture principles relate to enterprise principles?
o: Architecture principles sit above enterprise principles
Architecture principles sit below enterprise principles and embody their spirit
questions.e: Architecture principles govern the architecture work and sit below enterprise principles in the hierarchy, embodying their spirit.

questions.q: Which section of an architecture principle is described as the fundamental rule, kept short and crisp?
questions.e: The Statement is the fundamental rule, short and crisp. The four sections are Name, Statement, Rationale, and Implications.

questions.q: A principle that enables good-quality, consistent, enforceable decisions even in complex situations satisfies which criterion?
questions.e: Robust means the principle enables good-quality, consistent, and enforceable decisions even in complex or unforeseen situations.

questions.q: How does the TOGAF Standard define interoperability?
o: The ability to share information as well as services
The ability to reduce project cost
The ability to eliminate all architecture gaps
questions.e: Interoperability is the ability to share information as well as services. It is consolidated and reconciled as a step in Phase E.

questions.q: According to the notes, which dimension of the Business Transformation Readiness Assessment is the most important?
questions.e: The human factor is the most important dimension of the BTRA, because a change-averse culture can defeat even the best plan.

questions.q: Which categories of risk does the TOGAF Standard distinguish?
questions.e: TOGAF classifies risks by type as time (schedule), cost (budget), and scope. Initial and residual are the two risk levels; frequent and seldom are frequency ratings in the effect/frequency matrix.

questions.q: Every ADM architecture cycle begins with which phase?
questions.e: Every architecture cycle begins with Phase A: Architecture Vision. The Preliminary Phase is a pre-cycle setup; Requirements Management runs continuously; phases B-H can be iterated or entered at different points.

questions.q: Which landscape level has enterprise-wide breadth, low detail, and a long time horizon for executive direction setting?
questions.e: The Strategic level has enterprise-wide breadth, low detail, and a long horizon, used for executive-level direction setting.

questions.q: Which of the following is a stated benefit of architecture partitioning?
o: It removes the need for an Architecture Board
It enables parallelization of work across teams
It guarantees a single target architecture
questions.e: Partitioning enables parallelization of work, conflict management through clear responsibilities, reuse of modular segments, and reduced complexity.

questions.q: How many purposes frame the planning horizon, breadth, and depth of an architecture capability?
questions.e: There are four purpose capabilities: support Strategy, support Portfolio, support Project, and support Solution Delivery, each framing breadth, depth, and time period differently.

questions.q: Why must the ADM itself be governed?
o: Because the Open Group requires certification
Because the ADM creates, develops, and maintains the EA, and without governance you cannot tell whether projects move toward the target
Because governance replaces the need for stakeholders
Because it reduces the number of phases
questions.e: The ADM creates, develops, and maintains the EA (a change). Without governance you never reach the target because you cannot tell whether projects move toward it.

questions.q: Which of the following is a goal of the Architecture Board?
o: To ensure consistency of sub-architectures and set targets for reuse
To approve the corporate financial budget
To conduct the Business Transformation Readiness Assessment
questions.e: Architecture Board goals include ensuring consistency of sub-architectures, enforcing compliance, setting reuse targets, and providing an escalation capability.

questions.q: Which type of Architecture Contract is a statement of intent with partners such as system integrators to design and develop the EA?
questions.e: The Architecture Design and Development Contract is agreed with partners (system integrators, application providers) as a statement of intent to design and develop the EA.

questions.q: When an Architecture Compliance Review finds an issue, which recommendation grants temporary relief from compliance?
questions.e: A dispensation provides temporary relief from compliance. The other options are to enforce compliance or change the target architecture.

questions.q: Which standards does the TOGAF Standard draw on for its stakeholder, concern, view, and viewpoint terminology?
questions.e: TOGAF uses terminology from ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2015 for stakeholders, concerns, views, and viewpoints.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes a Solution Building Block (SBB)?
o: It is a logical, supplier-independent description of a required capability
It is a physical, implementation-specific component that delivers the solution
It shapes the specification of an ABB
It exists only in the Preliminary Phase
questions.e: An SBB is a physical, implementation-specific component that implements the capability. The ABB is logical and supplier-independent and shapes the SBB specification.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the Architecture Vision deliverable?
o: To act as the container for all core architectural artifacts
To provide a high-level, aspirational view of the capabilities and value to be delivered
questions.e: The Architecture Vision is a high-level, aspirational view of the capabilities and business value to be delivered, an early summary of the full Architecture Definition.

questions.q: Which deliverable is described as the quantitative companion, or 'twin brother,' of the Architecture Definition Document?
questions.e: The Architecture Requirements Specification is the quantitative view (measurable criteria) and the companion, or twin, of the qualitative Architecture Definition Document.

questions.q: When is the Architecture Definition Document (ADD) first drafted and when is it finalized?
o: Drafted in Preliminary, finalized in Phase A
Drafted in Phase A, finalized in Phase F
Drafted in Phase B, finalized in Phase G
Drafted in Phase E, finalized in Phase H
questions.e: The ADD is first drafted in Phase A, enriched in Phases B/C/D, and finalized in Phase F.
